description: A quality director must decide the disposition and controlled release plan for 4,800 returned battery modules after a software checksum alert, with input from test engineering, maintenance, warehouse logistics, and regulatory compliance.

shared_context.S1: A customer returned 4,800 battery modules after a software checksum alert appeared during its incoming inspection.
shared_context.S2: The modules are segregated in the returns area and cannot be shipped until Elena approves their disposition.
shared_context.S3: The modules are physically intact, and the customer has asked for a disposition decision today.
shared_context.S4: At the daily disposition board, Elena records a report from test engineering, maintenance, warehouse logistics, and regulatory compliance before signing the release plan.

PF1.text: Ravi's bench analysis found checksum mismatches in exactly 312 modules; the other 4,488 passed the checksum test. The 312 can be corrected by re-flashing and must then receive a 100% checksum verification. Ravi completed the analysis this morning, but the test report is still in his draft queue.

PF2.text: Marta confirmed that the programming rack's fixture calibration is out of tolerance and must be recalibrated before any re-flashing. The recalibration will take exactly 4 hours; she confirmed the duration with the equipment technician today, but the maintenance ticket has not yet been updated.

PF3.text: Jonas received the customer's dock instruction by email: the 4,488 passing modules must be staged in Zone B for pickup by exactly 14:00 tomorrow. He has not entered the instruction into the warehouse scheduling system.

PF4.text: Priya's review of the return shipment found that any battery modules transported after rework must be set to a state of charge no higher than exactly 30% and listed on a controlled battery manifest. She received the carrier's compliance interpretation today, but the regulatory note is awaiting her sign-off.

acceptance_conditions: Exactly 4,488 modules must be released without re-flashing, exactly 312 must be re-flashed, and zero must be scrapped.
The re-flashed modules must receive 100% checksum verification.
The programming rack must be recalibrated before re-flashing, with exactly 4 hours scheduled.
The 4,488 passing modules must be staged in Zone B by exactly 14:00 tomorrow.
Transport after rework must be limited to modules at no more than exactly 30% state of charge.
A controlled battery manifest must be explicitly required for the transported modules.
The checksum analysis must be cited as justification.

decisive_facts.why: The exact checksum analysis changes the disposition to 4,488 releases, 312 re-flashes, and zero scrap, and changes verification to 100% checksum verification.
The out-of-tolerance fixture changes the pre-reflash plan from no specified equipment work to exactly 4 hours of recalibration before re-flashing.
The customer's warehouse instruction changes staging from an unspecified location and time to Zone B by exactly 14:00 tomorrow.
The carrier's compliance interpretation changes transport controls to an exact 30% maximum state of charge and makes the controlled battery manifest requirement explicit.
